choices.text: Measure words like someone measuring blade distance—without insult, without plea.

respect.line: Kael tilts the helm a millimeter—almost respect. "…Discipline," he murmurs. "It isn't friendship."

choices.text: Accept mutual retreat and close the sentence without parade.

edge.line: "Then count on iron," says Kael, flat voice. Metal wakes in the air.

root.line: Edras's circle hisses beneath the snow. "Show me that your power knows how to stop before taking what it protects."

choices.text: Plant your feet and hold a gust between your hands without letting it touch the circle.
Explain that strength without limits destroys what it promised to guard.
Step into the wind and trust that you will know how to leave before it closes.
Press your palm against the circle's edge and pay for passage with blood.

stage2_clear.line: Edras relaxes one finger, but the wind still cuts your face. "Knowledge is not possession. Tell me why I should open my books."

choices.text: Lower your weapon and show that your strength can remain unused before an answer.
Say that learning creates an obligation; it does not turn the lesson into property.
Give Edras the name of the spell you most fear desiring.
Let the frozen seal burn your wrist and accept knowledge as a debt.

stage2_frayed.line: Your first answer unravels into white air. "One fracture," says Edras; the circle tightens around your ankles.

choices.text: Set your shoulders and hold all strength still while Edras measures your guard.
Correct the answer: knowledge received creates duty, never ownership.
Reveal the spell you fear desiring and let Edras judge the risk.
Press your wrist to the seal and pay the debt before knowing the lesson.

stage3_clear.line: The snowflakes stop between you, caught in the contrawind. "Every lesson changes the one who carries it. Show me that you accept the mark."

choices.text: Take the gust head-on and release it without striking back.
Name the change the lesson will make in you and accept its price.
Breathe in the circle's wind and accept that it will choose where to leave its mark.
Let the seal cut your skin and carry the scar as part of the lesson.

stage3_frayed.line: The wind finds the fracture and tears warmth from your chest. "Final measure," says Edras. "Control, understanding, or risk; choose without lying."

choices.text: Hold the gust in your trembling arms and release it away from the circle.
State precisely how the lesson will change you and what boundary you will not cross.
Open your guard to the contrawind and accept whatever mark comes.
Offer your palm to the seal and let the pain confirm your answer.

accepted.line: Edras closes his hand, and the wind falls like a sheathed blade. "You can learn without calling the lesson yours."

rejected.line: Edras cuts the air with two fingers; the circle closes and casts you into the snow. "Your power still mistakes hunger for right."
